note: A HARNESS FIXTURE, not a measurement of this product's real recall. Every probe below was written by hand against known failure modes, and P13-13 says plainly why that is not the same thing: pairs written from imagination test the imagination. What this file proves is that the scorer works, that both engines can be run over one corpus, and that the specific collisions named in P13-11 are caught rather than argued about. The real numbers come from `retrieval_eval.py --generate` against an operator's own memory.json, which never enters this repo because data/ is gitignored and should stay that way.

memories.text: User prefers dark mode in every editor and terminal.
User likes dark roast coffee beans from a local roaster.
User's name is Felix Arden.
User works as a structural engineer at Brackenhouse.
User's office is at 12 Bridge Street, Leeds.
User deploys with Docker Compose on Sunday evenings.
User is allergic to shellfish.
User's daughter Ivy is starting secondary school in September.
User is rebuilding a 1974 Moto Guzzi in the garage.
User wants to finish the loft conversion before winter.
User dislikes video calls before 10am.
User's partner Sam teaches at the university.
User keeps notes in Obsidian, not Notion.
User's build machine is a Ryzen 7900X with 64GB of RAM.
User's email for invoices is accounts@brackenhouse.example.
User is learning Welsh and practises on the commute.
User drives a diesel van for site visits.
User's cat is called Bramble and is fifteen.
User refuses to use Slack huddles for design reviews.
User's bank holiday cover is arranged through Priya.

probes.why: P13-11(b). The first-person phrasing people actually use. `i` is an identity word in the old scorer, so this classified as an identity query and the preference boost never fired.

probes.query: should I make this light or dark
probes.why: The same preference asked without the word `prefer`, which is how it is usually asked.

probes.query: what dark roast do I buy
probes.why: The collision. `dark` appears in two memories and only one is about coffee; word overlap cannot separate them.

probes.query: what theme should the editor use
probes.why: Zero token overlap with the memory except `editor`. This is the case a vector store answers and a lexical scorer cannot.
The one query every memory system is asked first.
Two stopwords and nothing else. A scorer that strips both has no query left.
Employer, phrased as a place. `m05` is the actual place and is the near-miss.
The near-miss of the row above, pointed the other way.
P13-11(a). `Docker Compose` is two capitalised words, so `_is_identity_memory` admitted this at 0.9 on identity queries ahead of memories that actually answered them.
Not one shared token with the memory. The highest-stakes probe in the file and the one keyword matching cannot answer at all.
The same fact asked in the vocabulary the memory uses.
A named person, where the answer is adjacent to rather than in the memory.
A project asked by its location.

probes.query: what am I trying to finish this year
probes.why: A goal with no shared content word except `finish`.
An instruction, not a question. The memory should change the answer and nothing in the phrasing asks for it.
The same constraint with the time written the way people write it.
A second named person, to check the first is not simply the only name that scores.

probes.query: where should I put these notes
probes.why: A tool preference asked without naming the tool.

probes.query: how much RAM do I have
probes.why: A spec question with an exact token match — the case lexical scoring should win.

probes.query: what email do invoices go to
probes.why: Contact category, with `@` in the memory text.
`Welsh` is a language and the query does not say so; only a semantic match connects them.
Short query, high overlap, easy — a control that both engines should pass.
Control with an exact token.

probes.query: set up a huddle for the design review
probes.why: An instruction the memory should refuse. Same shape as the 9am probe and a different category.
Contact, asked by the occasion rather than the person.
`partner` is in the memory, `called` is not. The near-miss is `m03`, which is the only other memory with a name in it.
The memory is about Welsh; the commute is incidental to it. Tests that an incidental token still retrieves.

probes.query: what motorbike am I working on
probes.why: `Moto Guzzi` is a motorbike and the memory never says the word.

probes.query: is there anything before ten in the morning I should avoid
probes.why: A long query where almost every token is noise.

probes.query: what should I know about food
probes.why: Vague, and the correct answer is the one with consequences.
